(sorry for my bad english and sorry for ma naive question)

I would like to use "measurementInvariance" with "effect coding". Because "measurementInvariance" use "cfa" function, I built effect coding for "cfa" and I have errors with measurementInvariance function. If I use a classic cfa I have no error (the resultts of CFAs are the exactly the same). See after codes and results.

Where is the problem with "effect coding" and "measurementInvariance"?

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance and effect coding : where is the problem?
parts:
Hi Hervé,

A couple of comments to try to help
  1. I don't think the measurementInvariance function is built to work with effects coding. The measurementInvariance function used the cfa command to fit all models, and to get effects coding to work you need to use the lavaan function (or override a lot of defaults on the cfa function)
  2. Part of the reason the measurementInvariance function works this way is that the method of scale setting (fixed factor, marker variable, effects coding) does not affect model fit of a model or tests of differences between models. The method of scale setting only affects the parameter estimates. So the results you saw with the second run (using the defaults) are the same as what you would see with effects coding
  3. There's an error in the effects coding syntax. For a multiple group model you need different labels (and different constraints) for each group. In addition, if you're working with effects coding you probably want to also specify constraints on the intercepts
Hope this helps,

Alex
